2611.08723.image_caption: Figure 2: Given task details, development examples, seed agentic pipeline, and objectives, DeCAF first identifies task-relevant optimization dimensions and generates diverse experimental hypotheses for each ( Divide ). Independent coding-agent sessions then optimize copies of the seed pipeline under dimension-specific edit constraints, producing Pareto candidates, execution trajectories, and structured findings ( Diagnose ). Finally, a synthesis optimizer combines compatible dimension-level findings and performs targeted cross-dimension revisions to produce a unified pipeline on the performance–cost–latency frontier with the help of a component or node-level diagnosis tool ( Compose ).

2611.09218.image_caption: Figure 4: BoxBox mechanism. The agent requests a review on demand, triggering a trap that transfers control to the kernel. The kernel then launches the review, validates revisions, and hot-reloads the runtime with preserved execution context and rollback if activation fails.

2611.09318.image_caption: Figure 1: Architecture of an RSI-ESA. Task evidence and component updates connect the execution and improvement loops. Persistent storage supplies task versions and experience.

2611.09472.image_caption: Figure 1: Readiness to learn differs from readiness to release. Removing both traces after training can leave skill B unsupported if only A has been learned. Engram verifies each skill: A uses verified weights and releases eligible records, while B retains external memory. Configured residuals remain; colored nodes represent behavior.

2611.08905.image_caption: Figure 1: Overview of our Skill-driven data synthesis method.

2611.08917.image_caption: Figure 4: Overview of the PRISM framework. (1) Skill primitive learning (§ 4 ): each atomic skill is fitted with its own rank- r r action-expert LoRA ( B i , A i ) (B_{i},A_{i}) , yielding a primitive bank of disjoint slots, frozen after atomic training. (2) Router learning from composite demonstrations : a prefix-conditioned router r θ r_{\theta} reads the VLM prefix h t h_{t} and emits a per-chunk mixture α ⁡ ( t ) \alpha(t) over the bank, supervised by per-chunk labels from a deterministic action-derived oracle 𝒜 \mathcal{A} . (3) Chunk-wise routed execution (inference): each LoRA-injected action-expert layer applies the routed mixture at the activation level (Eq. 5 ), producing an action chunk.

2611.09355.image_caption: Fig. 1: Illustration of memory noise and its effects on 3D manipulation. (a) Stored manipulation experiences for the same target object and subgoal contain varying non-target object details, introducing memory redundancy. (b) Using ECHO [ 6 ] for manipulation execution, we group memories by target and subgoal and randomly remove 30% of redundant entries differing only in non-target object details while preserving task-relevant experiences. On LIBERO-Long, in-distribution success rates decrease slightly from 93.50% to 93.25%, whereas out-of-distribution success rates improve from 92.78% to 94.67%. These results suggest that removing redundant memory details can improve out-of-distribution generalization while largely preserving in-distribution performance.

2611.09454.image_caption: Figure 1: The pipeline. A skill document s s is compiled into an adapter Δ s \Delta_{s} . The Executing Writer attaches Δ s \Delta_{s} (frozen) and a trainable writer ϕ \phi to the frozen base model θ \theta and generates a document s ^ \hat{s} . Recovery is scored by the share of the original’s key instructions that s ^ \hat{s} states and by whether s ^ \hat{s} still works when given to a model.

2611.09568.image_caption: Figure 1: Committee behavior for Qwen-2.5-1.5B-it on GSM8K. The committee size varies from one to five agents under independent sampling, after which the number of debate rounds is varied with five agents. Additional rounds increase agreement but do not improve consensus accuracy beyond the first exchange and can reduce correctness.

2611.09597.image_caption: Figure 1: Inactive rubrics and RuACT. (a) Illustration of unreachable, informative, and saturated rubrics and their distribution through training. (b) How RuACT recovers inactive rubrics: reward-verified guidance helps elicit missing behaviors, while finer-grained criticism exposes details for further improvement.

2611.09872.image_caption: Figure 2: Adaptation dynamics of Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct on the AMC benchmark. Left: fraction of problems in the initial majority-vote-solvable set that are recovered by the adapted policy. Middle: difference between the number of problems solved by the current policy and the initial majority-vote reference; the dashed line at zero denotes full recovery. Right: decomposition of the currently solved problems into those recovered from the initial majority-vote-solvable set and newly discovered solutions. The policy progressively recovers most initially available solutions while occasionally solving problems outside the initial set.

2611.09891.image_note: The automatically selected NVIDIA logo was replaced with a crop of the paper's Figure 1.

2611.09892.image_caption: Figure 1 : Zero-shot real-world manipulation with AMP1. AMP1 solves diverse, long-horizon manipulation tasks directly in the real world from a natural language instruction without task-specific fine-tuning or predefined skills. It devises complex strategies, such as ( A ) searching for hidden objects, ( B ) using a balance scale as a measuring instrument, ( C ) planning and executing a winning strategy in a game of chess, ( D ) combining non-prehensile and prehensile actions where a direct grasp is infeasible, and ( E ) manipulating articulated objects such as a kitchen cabinet door. Task instructions given to AMP1 for each episode are shown below the corresponding image sequence.

2611.08946.image_caption: Figure 1 : Flex-RSI at a glance. (a) The RSI loop. In each round, the executor edits the task solution, which is kept or reverted according to its score on held-out validation data; the improver then edits the harness, including the executor and itself. (b) The 24 tasks fall into six areas. Each tile shows an example task from one area, and its badge gives the number of tasks in that area. (c) Each dot is a task, placed by the score difference between the best and the worst model before (horizontal) and after (vertical) self-improvement; its height above the diagonal shows how much further apart the models end up. Blue: tasks in which the agent builds the solution. Gray: tasks whose solution is a single answer.

2611.09030.image_caption: Figure 1: Representative failure modes in Agentic Robotics. Left: Manipulation planning fails to select a grasp and approach strategy compatible with the downstream placement. Center: Motion planning fails to jointly reason about held-object geometry, obstacles, and clearance to produce a collision-free trajectory. Right: Deformable manipulation requires reasoning over object configuration and contact that is difficult to capture through local motion decisions.

2611.09348.image_caption: Figure 1: Victim optimization loop. Execution is scored against references; reflection proposes edits; validation and selection determine which candidate is persisted. The attacker supplies only tasks and references.

2611.09670.image_caption: Figure 2: One drawer start under three planners (true returns). Uniform averaging opens the drawer. Standard MPPI ( λ = 0.01 \lambda=0.01 ) on the 500-label scorer lifts the hand into a part of the workspace the data never visited; on the human-label scorer ( λ = 0.1 \lambda=0.1 ) it pulls in front of the handle without touching it.
